name: Pallu
overview: Pallu is a male descendant of the tribe of Reuben, identified specifically as a son of Reuben. He is noted among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his role in the early stages of Israel's sojourn in that land. His lineage is preserved in the biblical genealogies, including the listing of his descendants known as the Palluites.
namesAndTitles: The name Pallu means 'wonderful,' reflecting a proper name given at birth rather than a divine bestowal. This name is recorded in Genesis 46:9, providing a glimpse into the personal identity of this biblical figure.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pallu as a son of Reuben. Additionally, it is inferred that Eliab was his father, suggesting a generational link within the tribe of Reuben. Beyond these, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pallu's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel, particularly as a son of Reuben who accompanied the family into Egypt. His descendants, the Palluites, are enumerated among the tribes of Israel, underscoring the continuity of Reuben's lineage during the formative period of Israelite history in Egypt. This connection situates Pallu within God's sovereign plan for the nation of Israel.
